newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO welcome's Clinton pledeg on Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: NATO welcome's Clinton pledeg on Bosnia.

text.p: NATO said on Friday it welcomed the announcement by U.S. President Bill Clinton that the United States would participate in a follow up force in Bosnia next year.
In a statement, a NATO spokesman said the decision would make it easier for NATO to decide next week on what to propose for Bosnia after the mandate of its Implementation Force ends.
NATO ambassadors are expected to instruct their military on Monday to prepare for a force of betwen 25,000 and 30,000 troops to stay in Bosnia next year.
"The U.S. permanent representative (to the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) is expected to present detailed proposals (for Washington's commitment," the spokesman said.
In Washington, Clinton said the United States had agreed in principle to take part in a follow-up international military force to help cement peace in Bosnia next year.
He said this could amount to around 8,500 U.S. troops.
